description: Facts about the SysEx coverage table that no scan of the sources can read (ADR-MCP-006, DEC-MCP-038), read by juce/tools/generate_sysex_coverage.py. Each entry says why it is here. Do not list here what a scan finds by itself: the script refuses a stale entry.

table32.note: The alternative sections of the specification are in neither the item catalogue (juce/akm/data/items.json), nor the spec's item list, nor the code: the index forms (2A, 2C, 2E, 32) put the index of the item in the first two bytes and are otherwise the section they point to; the blocked forms (38, 3A, 3C, 3E) take several requests, three data bytes each, in one message and answer with one REPLY. They are rows of the table so that the gap is seen (RQ-MCP-058).

sent_by_the_session.reason: The server's own session sends these at its opening and its closing, from the launch option --screen (and the checksum mode): they are the sampler's SysEx configuration for the session, not something an assistant asks for, so no tool carries them

generic_akm.reason: reads one Get item for every keygroup of the current program (keygroup 0); the parameter tools give it the keygroup items
reads one Get item for the four zones (zone 0); the parameter tools give it the zone items
reads one Get item for every zone of every keygroup (zone 0 and keygroup 0); the parameter tools give it the zone items

tool_options.reason: list_disks sends the refresh of the disk list only with its refresh argument, which needs --allow-disk-refresh as well (it hung a real S5000)

notes.note: create_program sends Create Program with keygroups (&03: a number of keygroups, 1 to 99, and a name) and always gives the number of keygroups; the spec does not say how many keygroups &02 creates.
The parameter tools send Select Keygroup (&01) before each read or write, so the server sets the keygroup and never asks which one is selected.
list_samples sends Get the names of all of the samples in memory (&12): every name in one message, instead of one message per sample.
The server never tests a disk handle: select_disk checks the handle it is given against the list that Get list of all connected disks (&05) returns, and refuses one that is not in it.
The number of disks is the length of the list that Get list of all connected disks (&05) returns.

Get list of all connected disks (&05) gives, for every disk, its type, its format, whether it is writable and its name; list_disks sends it with Get index of current disk (&08), which says which one is current.
Get list of all connected disks (&05) gives the type of every disk, and list_disks shows it.
Get list of all connected disks (&05) gives the format of every disk; list_disks sends it with Get index of current disk (&08), which says which one is current.
list_disk_contents sends Get the names of all of the sub-folders in the current folder (&12): every name in one message, instead of one per folder.
list_disk_contents sends Get the names of all of the files in the current folder (&22): every name in one message, instead of one per file.
The server gives the sampler a file's name for the operations that take one, and lists the names with Get the names of all of the files (&22); it never asks for the index of a file.
list_scenelists sends Get Current Scenelist's Index (&13) and Get the name of Scenelist by index (&11): the current name is the name at the current index.
list_song_files sends Get Current Songfile's Index (&13) and Get the name of Songfile by index (&11): the current name is the name at the current index.

A batch read: the spec's &47 reads the parameters &20 to &2B of one part in a single message. get_multi_parameters sends one message per parameter asked for (&20 to &2B), so the values are the same and the messages more numerous.
A batch read: the spec's &48 reads the mute and solo of all the parts in a single message. get_multi_parameters sends Get Part Mute (&21) and Get Part Solo (&22) for each part asked for.
A batch read: the spec's &34 reads the parameters &30 to &33 of the current sample in a single message. get_sample_parameters sends one message per parameter asked for.
A batch read: the spec's &4B reads the parameters &40 to &4A of the current sample in a single message. get_sample_parameters sends one message per parameter asked for.

A test of the link: the sampler returns the four data bytes it received (the spec: useful when debugging a controlling program). The server needs no such test: its session opens with Query (&00), and get_status sends &10, &13 and &14, whose answers show that the link works.
The number by which a MIDI program change selects the program (1 to 128), or off. AKM has setProgramNumber; the server has set_multi_program_number for multis only.
Reads the number by which a MIDI program change selects the current program. AKM has getProgramNumber; the server has no tool that reads a program's number.
Reads the number of every program in memory. AKM has getAllProgramNumbers; the server has no tool that reads a program's number.

The position of the current program in memory. list_programs gives the positions from Get the names of all Programs (&19) and the server finds the current program by its name (&13); for samples, multis, scenelists and song files the server sends a message that gives the position of the current one (&13, &42, &13, &13), and for programs it does not. AKM has getProgramIndex.
The user tuning of a program: a tuning offset for each of the 12 notes (24 data bytes), used when its tune template is USER. Described in the catalogue; no AKM function and no tool.
Reads the user tuning of the current program (the tuning offset of each of the 12 notes). Described in the catalogue; no AKM function and no tool.

How many parts (32, 64 or 128) the multis created afterwards have. AKM has setNewMultiPartCount; create_multi does not set it, so a new multi has the number of parts the sampler is set to (32 on the sampler tried).

The program number of every multi. The server gives it for the current multi only, as the read-back of set_multi_program_number, so reading another multi's number means selecting it first. AKM has getAllMultiProgramNumbers.

The number of parts of every multi. list_multis gives it for the current multi only (Get the Number of Parts in the Current Multi, &44), so reading another multi's count means selecting it first. AKM has getAllMultiPartCounts.

list_parameters.sends_nothing: it reads the parameter catalogue and does not talk to the sampler
